### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/connector-app-github`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/apps/connector-github/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via providerConfig (symbol, a field of const object GitHubMcpConnector))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via providerConfig (symbol, a field of const object GitHubMcpConnector))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/odata-datasources.mdx`  _(via providerConfig (symbol, a field of const object GitHubMcpConnector))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via providerConfig (symbol, a field of const object GitHubMcpConnector))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via providerConfig (symbol, a field of const object GitHubMcpConnector))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/apps/connector-github/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8784ccbce0ee549da50b8cf43531c9c5bb2aa9f1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `87f7ebf9381f14fed3f8e6508c87b58025a70fd3` — the merge of head `9f1340c688079e25029dd1505c55ee3b8cb4bf67` into base `8784ccbce0ee549da50b8cf43531c9c5bb2aa9f1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 87f7ebf9381f14fed3f8e6508c87b58025a70fd3 && git checkout 87f7ebf9381f14fed3f8e6508c87b58025a70fd3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8784ccbce0ee549da50b8cf43531c9c5bb2aa9f1 9f1340c688079e25029dd1505c55ee3b8cb4bf67 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8784ccbce0ee549da50b8cf43531c9c5bb2aa9f1 && git merge --no-ff 9f1340c688079e25029dd1505c55ee3b8cb4bf67

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8784ccbce0ee549da50b8cf43531c9c5bb2aa9f1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8784ccbce0ee549da50b8cf43531c9c5bb2aa9f1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · round 1 · head `9f1340c6` · 2026-11-08T18:35Z

**Verdict: ACCEPT.**

- **Pins verbatim.** The two `toolsSnapshot` values are exactly the two 64-hex digests in #30116 comment 6691107153 (seat re-read). `computeMcpToolsSnapshot` over the committed fixture reproduces both, so the fixture and the pins cannot drift apart silently.
- **Pin-set digest.** The seat re-ran the README's `printf … | sha256sum` line and got `e922e2420b05707fb3ec9df270009da30d57177c297a6d7c3ee0b4ccbbad7516`, which matches the README and `pinSetDigest`.
- **Offline test (card's bullet 2).** `listing.test.ts` › `connector-github tool pins` refuses a missing pin, a pin that is not 64 lowercase hex, and a pin on a tool not in `include`. The ablations were measured red, then restored clean. No live call is made.
- **Provenance (card's bullet 3).** No manifest field carries listing provenance in this repo today; Stripe and DocuSign keep it as a README section, and this PR follows that shape. The token scope (broader than read-only) is recorded as measured, per triage 6723942187.
- **Forced edit.** `boot.test.ts`'s fake server now serves the measured definitions. This is required: the old stand-ins would, correctly, trip the drift check.
- **Claim lines.** `Clause-②: no` holds (data on the existing key `toolsSnapshot`). `Metadata-protocol: none` holds. `skip-changeset` holds because the package is `"private": true`.

**Rulings on open_questions:**
1. commit → **A.** The publisher or the ingestion records it. A manifest provenance key would be a spec/marketplace format change: outside this lane and outside this card.
2. Recipe → **A.** The rules plus the `printf | sha256sum` line are enough for cloud ingestion to recompute the digest. Exporting a shared `canonicalJson` is not needed for this card.

Landing: after CI is green on `9f1340c6`.
